pull.title: fix(release): verify final branch reference identity
pull.body:
Production release validation could skip the final live-source check when using executed qualification, and the shared branch guard compared only the extracted SHA. Validate the complete branch reference and require the late check in the protected release context while preserving offline local qualification and exact recorded CI run/attempt checks.

The five-file change preserves the newer final prepare hook, source-CI delegation, package qualification, publisher and prerelease controls. CI-proof test doubles remain mode-specific; a private omission mutation is refused.

Validation: 79 source-CI cases, 28 live-reference cases, four real wrapper scenarios, full pure publisher checks, 68 selected Python cases, legacy/v2 workflow assertions, a resource-free Release build with no warnings or errors, and the three controlled Aspire equality cases passed. The earlier 71-case artifact check is retained separately. Hosted source CI and genuine publication remain separate gates.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core release publication guards and GitHub API trust boundaries; mistakes could block releases or weaken pre-publish source verification.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Release source checks are tightened** so publication cannot rely on a matching commit SHA alone or skip the final live verification when legacy **executed** qualification runs in production.
> 
> `verify-g4-release-source.sh` now validates the **entire** Git ref payload from the API (`ref`, canonical `url`, commit `object` type/SHA/urls), rejecting foreign repos, wrong refs, tags, or malformed JSON even when the digest happens to match.
> 
> `Assert-CurrentReleaseSource` still stays **offline** for local executed qualification, but when `GITHUB_JOB` is **release** it requires the full protected context (Builds repo, `main`/`prerelease`, `workflow_dispatch`, matching `build-release.yml` ref/SHA, valid run id/attempt), always runs the bash late guard, and only passes **EXPECTED_CI_RUN_*** env vars for **ci** mode—not for executed legacy releases.
> 
> Tests were expanded across the bash guard (malformed live refs), source-CI PowerShell (release-context executed path + foreign env rejection), and publisher fixtures (executed releases must invoke live guard once; CI proof expectations are mode-aware).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 43adaa5d30437bec89f9485d414b1f92342b617c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

Your code is checked against an extensive set of rules that cover many attributes of code, such as maintainability, reliability, and security issues, on each merge/pull request.

For those requiring US-based hosting, [SonarQube Cloud US](https://sonarqube.us/) offers the perfect alternative. If you need data residency outside the US or within the EU, [SonarQube Cloud](https://sonarcloud.io/) with this GitHub app is the ideal solution.

SonarQube Cloud integrates seamlessly into your GitHub workflow and provides clear guidance for resolving any code quality and security issues detected. The majority of popular languages can be analyzed automatically; no configuration is required!

With [SonarQube Cloud](https://sonarcloud.io/github), you get:

-   Fast, precise static analysis and feedback on your code
    
-   Support for popular languages, frameworks, and IaC tools
    
-   Free analysis for open-source projects and private projects up to max 50k LoC
    
-   Automatic analysis of pull requests and branches with results reported inline
    
-   IDE Support with [SonarQube for IDE](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarlint/) integration
    
-   Quality Gate (added as a GitHub check) acting at two different levels - first, preventing you from merging pull requests that contain issues - and later, helping you to release only clean, safe code
    
-   Sign up for SonarQube free tier and begin scanning your private and public repositories
    

A [GitHub Action](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/sonarcloud-scan) is available in the marketplace to make it easy for you (for projects where automatic analysis isn't available). SonarQube Cloud also integrates smoothly with Jenkins, CircleCI, TravisCI, CirrusCI, and many other tools.

A free tier is available that allows you to explore the benefits of SonarQube Cloud using your public and private repositories. We also provide a no-commitment, [14-day trial](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarcloud/signup/) of SonarQube Cloud Team for unlimited team members, up to 1.9M LoC, AI CodeFix recommendations, and more. No need to speak with a sales rep or request a license key - get automatic code analysis results on your private projects in minutes! Want to see more examples of SonarCloud in action? You can [explore current Open Source projects in SonarCloud](https://sonarcloud.io/explore/projects?sort=-analysis_date) that are using the [Clean as You Code](https://www.sonarsource.com/solutions/our-unique-approach/) methodology.

What are you waiting for? SonarQube Cloud helps you consistently deliver cleaner, secure software that future developers will appreciate and your users will love. Start writing Clean Code. [Now](https://www.sonarsource.com/products/sonarcloud/signup/)!
